blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: model — Representation of a real-world concept.

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.text: Class Loan models a single loan request, containing a student and book title initialised in its constructor.

blocks.title: Model
blocks.text: Queue<Loan> stores objects in requested service order. Enqueue adds a new request and Dequeue retrieves oldest.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: For a more complete system, use a Dictionary keyed by unique loan ID, validation and tests; do not treat a name as necessarily unique. A queue exists only while the program keeps it in memory; a text file can persist loan records. In OCR examination pseudocode, openWrite plus writeLine writes a file (overwriting existing contents), while openRead plus readLine retrieves lines. Always close() the file.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain
blocks.text: Queue is FIFO, so the first enqueued request is processed first.

blocks.title: Worked example · Why a file?
blocks.text: Unlike the queue, the text file can hold a record across program runs. openWrite creates a write stream and replaces any existing contents of the target file; it is not an append operation.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: A dictionary retrieves by key; it does not enforce FIFO service order.

blocks.title: Predict what is printed
blocks.text: Identify the role of endOfFile() and the effect of each readLine() call.

blocks.title: Follow two reads
blocks.text: The first call prints Ada,Holes; the second prints Ben,Dune. The file position advances after each read.

blocks.title: Stop safely
blocks.text: Once no unread lines remain, endOfFile() is true, the loop stops, and f.close() releases the reader. This example reads text; it does not reconstruct Loan objects automatically.
